title: Burst Absorber Architecture and Decision Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:

This playbook describes the Burst Absorber pattern — an operational architecture and decision procedure used to protect Redwood Inference production services from short-term traffic spikes and cascading failures while preserving customer-level SLOs and minimizing error-budget consumption. It covers the design rationale, key components, alerting thresholds, step-by-step on-call runbook for mitigation, traffic simulation guidance, capacity planning heuristics, and post-incident review criteria.

When to use this playbook:

- Sudden traffic spikes that are transient (minutes -> tens of minutes) but risk saturating GPU inference pools.
- Repeated short failures in downstream dependencies causing amplified retry storms.
- During large customer launches or marketing-driven traffic surges where graceful degradation is required.

Architecture overview (text diagram):

Edge (API Gateway / Regional LB) -> Adaptive Throttle Layer (Envoy/Service) -> Burst Absorber (buffer + tokenized rate controller) -> Inference Frontend -> GPU Pool

Key components and responsibilities:

1) Adaptive Throttle Layer (edge-level):
   - Operates per-route and per-customer token-buckets.
   - Primary function is to reject obvious abuse and smooth microbursts before they reach the absorber.
   - Example: Envoy local rate limit + per-route header-per-customer key.

2) Burst Absorber service (stateless controller + small persistent buffer):
   - Accepts traffic at a configurable ingress rate and holds short-lived request tokens in an in-memory queue for controlled release.
   - Provides backpressure to clients using Retry-After and 429s with structured diagnostics.
   - Implements a tokenized error-budget mechanism (see SLO coupling below).

3) Inference Frontend (service-level):
   - Batches requests and manages KV cache and ordering for GPU inference.
   - Exposes health / capacity endpoints used by the absorber to adjust drain rates.

SLO coupling and error-budget policy:

- Primary SLO: 99th percentile request latency for text-generation endpoints <= 300ms (endpoint: /v1/generate).
- Secondary SLO: Success rate >= 99.5% per rolling 7d window.
- Error budget policy for bursts: The absorber maintains a small "burst budget" equal to 0.5% of weekly error budget for a service. If burst budget consumption exceeds this, the absorber switches to strict-reject mode (no buffering) and routes to fallback model variants.

Operational thresholds and alerts (prometheus / pager rules):

1) Early warning alert (P2): sustained incoming rate > 4x baseline for 3m with queue depth > 25
   - PromQL (example):
     sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="edge",route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (job) > 4 * avg_over_time(sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="edge",route="/v1/generate"}[1m]))[1h:]) and absorber_queue_depth > 25

2) Burst absorption alert (P1 - page): absorber_queue_depth > 100 OR burst_budget_burn_rate > 0.01/min for 2m
   - PromQL: absorber_queue_depth > 100 OR increase(burst_budget_consumed_total[2m]) > 0.02

3) Capacity saturation alert (P0): observed GPU_utilization >= 92% for 5m and backpressure_in_effect == true

Runbook: responding to a burst event (step-by-step)

1) Triage (first 3 minutes)
   - Confirm alert source and scope via Slack channel #sre-ops and the service dashboard. Identify affected regions and customer segments.
   - Check absorber metrics: queue depth, token drain rate, burst_budget_remaining, downstream 5xx rate.
   - Command: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=burst-absorber -o wide

2) Immediate containment (3-10 minutes)
   - If queue depth increasing and burst_budget_consumption > 0.4 of its allocation, enable strict-reject mode: set absorber.config.rejection_mode = true via feature-flag CLI or HTTP API.
   - HTTP API example: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/absorber/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"rejection_mode":true, "rejection_code":429}'
   - Apply temporary per-customer rate caps for the identified noisy customers using the Adaptive Throttle Layer (Envoy config push).

3) Short-term mitigation (10-30 minutes)
   - Scale inference frontends (horizontal) if autoscaler recommended replicas < target and GPU pool has available headroom: kubectl scale deploy/inference-frontend --replicas=TARGET_REPLICAS.
   - If GPU pool cannot scale or latency still rising, flip traffic to lighter, compatible model variant (e.g., "gpt-lite-v1") using routing rule: set route.model_override = "gpt-lite-v1" for affected customer IDs.

4) Recovery and verification (30-90 minutes)
   - Once queue depth < 10 and backend 5xx < 0.1% for 15 minutes, gradually restore absorber to buffered mode: set rejection_mode=false and increase drain_rate by +10% every 2 minutes.
   - Validate SLO telemetry for the last hour and ensure no long-tail latency regressions at p99.

5) Communication and escalation
   - Post an incident summary in the #incident-ops channel within 60 minutes including: cause hypothesis, mitigation steps taken, current impact, and customer-facing notes.
   - If mitigation requires customer-visible changes (model downgrade, throttling) notify Customer Success with a short explainer and list of affected customers.

Traffic simulation guidance (game-day / pre-release verification):

- Use the traffic-play tool to reproduce burst profiles. Example command:
  traffic-play --target https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate --rps 12000 --burst-pattern="gaussian,peak=60000,duration=120" --customer-header X-Customer-Id:playtest-1

- Metrics to validate in simulation:
  - absorber_queue_depth max < 200
  - time_to_recover_to_baseline < 10m after burst peak
  - no more than 0.3% additional error budget consumed by simulated test

Capacity planning heuristics for burst absorption:

- Buffer sizing rule of thumb: buffer_size = max(ceil(peak_request_rate * 2s), 100) but cap at 10k items to avoid excessive memory.
- Drain rate tuning: start with drain_rate = baseline_rps * 1.2 and ramp up as frontends signal readiness.
- Reserve 15% of GPU pool for emergency drain traffic (set via cluster taints / reservation labels).

Configuration table (examples):

| config_key | default | description | owner |
| absorber.buffer_size | 500 | max queued requests held for smoothing | eng-sre/platform |
| absorber.burst_budget_weekly | 0.5% | % of weekly error budget usable for burst absorption | eng-sre/slo-team |
| absorber.rejection_mode | false | when true the absorber returns immediate 429s instead of buffering | eng-sre/platform |
| edge.per_customer_rate_limit_default | 120 rps | default per-customer fallback cap | eng-sre/edge |

Deployment and safe-rollout checklist:

1) Feature flag gating: new absorber logic must be behind a flag scoped to non-prod then progressively to 10% prod traffic.
2) Canary validation: run traffic-play scenarios on canary and compare p95/p99 to baseline.
3) Automated rollback: implement a kill-switch that sets absorber.rejection_mode=true and reverts route model overrides.

Instrumenting post-incident reviews and RCA standards (SRE incident review integration):

- Required artifacts for RCA: absorber logs (last 6 hours), traffic-play reproduction config, Prometheus query snapshots, and list of feature flag changes in the incident window.
- RCA timeline must include: detection timestamp, mitigation start, mitigation full effect, and recovery timestamp.
- Measure regression risk score: combine (burst_budget_burn_pct * 0.6) + (avg_p99_latency_regression_ms / 1000 * 0.4). Incidents with score > 0.5 require cross-team remediation plan.

On-call escalation matrix (quick):

- P2: on-call SRE -> page primary responder (15 mins)
- P1: on-call SRE -> page primary + on-call infra (5 mins)
- P0: immediate page to SRE lead + Eng Product + Customer Success (1 min)

Ownership and contacts:

- Absorber service owner: eng-sre/platform (primary on-call: @sre-platform)
- Edge throttling owner: eng-developer-experience/edge team
- SLO policy owner: eng-sre/slo-team

Postmortem and remediation playbook (when burst causes measurable SLO burn):

1) Create postmortem within 48 hours with the required artifacts.
2) Schedule a 1-hour remediation triage with owners present.
3) Implement one of: increase baseline capacity by 10%, refine per-customer caps, or redesign backlog eviction strategy.

Appendix: useful snippets and configs

- Example Envoy rate limit descriptor (YAML):
  descriptors:
    - key: customer-id
      value: "%REQ(X-Customer-Id)%"
      rate_limit:
        unit: MINUTE
        requests_per_unit: 7200

- Example Prometheus expression to compute burst_budget_remaining:
  burst_budget_total_weekly - increase(burst_budget_consumed_total[7d])

- Example absorber health endpoints:
  GET /_internal/absorber/health -> {"status":"ok", "queue_depth": 42, "burst_budget_remaining": 0.32}

References and related docs:

- Service capacity governance and error budget handbook (links in related_pages)
- Runbook: slo-driven-autoscale-hybrid-inference-runbook-2026

Notes and open decisions (work items):

- Evaluate integrating HSM-backed tokens for per-customer tokens to simplify cross-region consistency (owner: eng-platform).
- Assess viability of adding a persistent redis-backed overflow queue for very large, but legitimate, bulk-batch requests (owner: eng-serving-runtime).

End of document.
